why_separate: the declared F0 taxonomy text used this set-based form before the 2026-09-12 adjudication; the frozen F1 schema uses the single-q tail predicate (divergence D1). F1 now carries ONE canonical predicate and this reading is registered as a VARIANT (parent_class + variant_id), not a class, so neither direction is silently conflated.

changes.to: AF-WCC-VAC-GEN with variant SET applied (variant_id SET, parent_class AF-WCC-VAC-GEN; NOT a class id)

changes.from: a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter is visible from I+ iff there exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M. Visibility is a property of the singular END of the geodesic, so the tail formulation is used; requiring the whole geodesic to lie in J^-(q) would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted]
changes.to: a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter is visible-from-I-plus-in-the-set-sense iff gamma([0,T)) is contained in the union of J^-(q) over q in I+ (intersected with M). This is the SET-based reading of the F0 taxonomy: it is implied by, and strictly stronger than, the single-q tail predicate.

changes.from: there is NO visible_singularity_from_I_plus: for every future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma of finite affine length, for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail gamma([t0,T)) is NOT contained in J^-(q) intersect M - no single point of I+ causally precedes the singular end of gamma. This is NOT equivalent to 'gamma is contained in B = M minus J^-(I+)': B-containment is strictly stronger, and a geodesic may begin in J^-(I+) and end in the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted; the earlier 'i.e. inside B' equivalence was false]
changes.to: there is NO such visible singularity: every future-inextendible causal geodesic of finite affine length is NOT contained in the union of J^-(q) over q in I+, i.e. it lies outside J^-(I+) as a set. This is strictly stronger than the single-q negation and MUST NOT be interchanged with it.

changes.from: forall r in D0 exists G_r comeager forall D in G_r: AF_{I+}(M_D) and complete(I+_D) and not exists visible_singularity_from_I_plus(M_D)
changes.to: forall r in D0 exists G_r comeager forall D in G_r: AF_{I+}(M_D) and complete(I+_D) and not exists set_visible_singularity_from_I_plus(M_D)
changes.from_previous_revision: forall (s,delta) in D0 exists G_{s,delta} comeager forall D in G_{s,delta}: AF_{I+}(M_D) and complete(I+_D) and not exists visible_singularity_from_I_plus(M_D)

changes.from: non_vacuity is a well-formedness condition on the class (it must admit data with a future-incomplete development), NOT a conjunct of the mathematical statement above. [R1 minor]
changes.to: non_vacuity is a well-formedness condition on the class (it must admit data with a future-incomplete development), NOT a conjunct of the mathematical statement above. [R1 minor] The visibility predicate is the SET-based one; binding a single-q result to this variant, or a set-based result to AF-WCC-VAC-GEN, is class leakage.

falsifier: exhibit an incomplete causal geodesic contained in the union J^-(I+) whose every tail escapes each single J^-(q): that datum satisfies variant SET's negation while leaving AF-WCC-VAC-GEN's predicate satisfied, demonstrating that the two readings differ (and that D1 was a real divergence).
